content.text: As a performance optimization, Swift lets you create some properties only when they are needed. As an example, consider this `FamilyTree` struct – it doesn’t do much, but in theory creating a family tree for someone takes a long time:
We might use that `FamilyTree` struct as a property inside a `Person` struct, like this:

But what if we didn’t always need the family tree for a particular person? If we add the `lazy` keyword to the `familyTree` property, then Swift will only create the `FamilyTree` struct when it’s first accessed:
So, if you want to see the “Creating family tree!” message, you need to access the property at least once:

title: Lazy properties
question: Which of these are true?
hint: Lazy properties are an important performance optimization, because they let us run code only once and only when it's needed.

correct.answer: Lazy properties are created only when first accessed.
correct.reason: This is exactly how lazy properties work.

correct.answer: You can assign lazy properties by calling a method.
correct.reason: This can help keep your code more organized.

correct.answer: Lazy properties are created using the `lazy` keyword.
Lazy properties can be used inside any kind of structs.
A lazy property can be an instance of a different struct.
Lazy properties are a performance optimization.
correct.reason: They are created only when needed, and so might never be created.

wrong.answer: Lazy properties never do any work.
wrong.reason: Lazy properties can be accessed just like regular properties.

wrong.answer: Lazy properties only work with strings.
wrong.reason: You can use any data type you need.

wrong.answer: Lazy properties are created when your app finishes.
wrong.reason: They are created when first accessed.

wrong.answer: Lazy properties act like property observers.
wrong.reason: Lazy properties are quite different from property observers.

wrong.answer: Lazy properties must be created using `self`
Lazy properties can use trailing closure syntax.
wrong.reason: Only functions and methods can use trailing closure syntax.
